stem: Which one of the following statements is true according to the author?

options.label: A
options.text: Agriculture has always been part of all civilizations.

options.label: B
options.text: Not all civilizations have undergone the processes of agriculture.

options.label: C
options.text: Agriculture gave birth to new civilizations.

options.label: D
options.text: Communities discontinued agriculture to become civilizations.

reasoning: The passage opens: 'no civilization can become one without passing through the stage of agriculture.' So agriculture has been part of every civilization, which is option (a). Option (b) says the opposite, that some civilizations never went through agriculture. Option (c) goes too far: agriculture is a necessary stage, but the passage does not say it gave birth to civilizations, since not all agricultural societies became civilizations. Option (d) is not stated anywhere.

reasoning: Chronological: after schooling (S1, 1930s), S (BA 1953, BBC 1956), R (joined NBC 1954, became Director External Broadcasting), P (during the Civil War), Q (after the war, Senior Research Fellow), then S6 summary. The natural educational-then-career progression gives SRPQ.

P: It organizes our knowledge and gives us a place from which to argue.
Q: This mental model is, he says, like a giant filing cabinet.
R: It contains a slot for every item of information coming to us.

reasoning: S1 introduces the mental model; Q likens it to a filing cabinet; R explains it has a slot for every item of information; P says it organizes our knowledge and gives a place to argue; S closes with the Schumacher quote leading into S6. Sequence QRPS.

stem:
S1: Britain was the first country to experience modern industrialization.
S6: This gave people a wider choice for ways to spend their earnings and expanded the market for the sale of goods.
P: This meant that the kingdom had common laws, a single currency and a market that was not fragmented by local authorities and uneven taxation.
Q: It had been politically stable since the seventeenth century, with England, Wales and Scotland unified under a monarchy.
R: By then a large section of the people received their income in the form of wages and salaries than in goods.
S: By the end of the seventeenth century, money was widely used as the medium of exchange.
reasoning: S1 says Britain industrialized first. Q gives a reason: it had been politically stable since the seventeenth century. P draws the result with 'This meant': common laws, one currency and a single market. S says money was widely used as the medium of exchange by the end of that century. R follows with 'By then', the time S has just named: many people were paid in wages rather than goods. S6 says this gave people more ways to spend their earnings and widened the market. The sequence is QPSR.

stem:
S1: For several million years, humans lived by hunting wild animals and gathering wild plants.
S6: As a result, conditions were favourable for the growth of grasses such as wild barley and wheat.
P: This led to the development of farming and pastoralism as a way of life.
Q: This change took place because the last ice age came to an end about 13,000 years ago and with that warmer, wetter conditions prevailed.
R: Then, between 10,000 and 4,500 years ago, people in different parts of the world learnt to domesticate certain plants and animals.
S: The shift from foraging to farming was a major turning point in the human history.
reasoning: S1 says humans lived by hunting and gathering for millions of years. R follows with 'Then': people learnt to domesticate plants and animals. P says 'This led to' farming and pastoralism. S sums up the shift from foraging to farming as a turning point. Q explains 'This change': the last ice age ended and the climate became warmer and wetter. S6 gives the result with 'As a result': conditions favoured wild grasses such as barley and wheat. The sequence is RPSQ.

stem:
S1: All governments claim eternal consistency and success.
S6: Diplomacy offers choices, and those choices must be negotiated with other sovereign actors.
P: Choices involved uncertainty, risk and immediacy; those who must take the choices operate in the contemporary political milieu.
Q: And yet the essence of governance is choice.
R: Nowhere is this more true than in foreign policy decision-making.
S: Some even claim omniscience.
reasoning: S1 says governments claim consistency and success. S goes further: 'Some even claim omniscience.' Q turns with 'And yet': governing is really about choice. P describes choices: they bring uncertainty, risk and urgency. R says 'Nowhere is this more true than in foreign policy decision-making.' S6 follows on from foreign policy: diplomacy offers choices that must be negotiated with other countries. The sequence is SQPR.

stem:
S1: Buddhism continued to spread into many lands of Asia during the period of 5th and 6th century.
S6: He translated several scriptural commentaries into Pali and wrote a work called the Visuddhimagga, which soon attained the status of a classic work on Theravada doctrine and meditation.
P: While this can be understood as a part of larger processes of cultural interaction, especially trade, a key role was played by monks.
Q: We know a little bit about some of them, but there must have been countless men whose commitment to the Buddhist path gave them the courage and determination to persevere in the face of the long, hard journey to India and back.
R: Buddhism had made its way to Sri Lanka many centuries earlier, during the time of Ashoka, and a thriving Buddhist community soon took root.
S: In the 5th century, the monk Buddhaghosha travelled to Sri Lanka.
reasoning: S1 says Buddhism spread across Asia. P says monks played a key role in this. Q follows with 'some of them': we know a little about some monks, but countless others made the journey. R turns to Sri Lanka, where Buddhism had arrived in Ashoka's time. S names one monk: Buddhaghosha went to Sri Lanka in the 5th century. S6 says 'He' translated commentaries into Pali and wrote the Visuddhimagga, and 'He' needs S just before it. The sequence is PQRS.

stem: "Those who sowed the seeds last season will reap the harvest this season," said the leader to her followers.

options.label: A

reasoning: The strict rule for reported speech shifts every tense back and every time word away from the present: 'sowed' becomes 'had sown', 'will reap' becomes 'would reap', 'last season' becomes 'the previous season' and 'this season' becomes 'that season'. Option (c) is the only one that makes all four changes, so it is the keyed answer. The item is not clean, though. (a) makes every change except 'sowed' to 'had sown', and many grammars allow a simple past to stay unshifted; (a) also uses the correct 'said to her followers that', while (c) uses 'addressed her followers that', which is not idiomatic. (b) and (d) leave 'this season' unchanged.
